scenario: WIBTA for declining to be a groomsman in a close friends wedding? | A friend I’ve known for about 10 years or so is getting married next month, and invited me out to dinner to “catch up” since it had been about a year since we hung out last. We chatted over dinner and after a while he asked me if I liked Kershaw knives. We’re both pretty outdoorsy and dabble a bit in the prepper life so it wasn’t an odd question to ask, and I responded with yes. He then slid a knife to me and asked me to check it out. I open it up and check out the craftsmanship, noticing an engraving on the blade. It was engraved with “ *lastname’s* wedding : 4-25-20 - Groomsman” and he had a big smile on his face when he saw I noticed it. He then asked me excitedly to be a groomsman for his wedding. Some additional context before getting into this next part. I’m the one who set him up with his fiancé, who happens to be very close friends to my ex, and you can kinda see where this is going. My ex was very mentally and emotionally abusive to me over a long period of time. It took me a while to realize it and I dumped her 2 years ago with no contact afterward at all. She is going to be a bridesmaid in their wedding and I’m not sure I want to put myself in that environment. Would I be the asshole for declining to be a part of their wedding? He asked me so last minute and I feel like it would mean a lot for me to be there for him and his soon-to-be wife.

Diwali is just around the corner! Don't worry, I'm here to help you prioritize your tasks. Considering you have a lot to do, let's break it down into manageable chunks. This will help you visualize what you need to buy or create. **Decorations (Next 2-3 days)** 1. **Lighting**: Focus on setting up the main lighting fixtures, such as fairy lights, candles, or string lights. This will help create a warm ambiance and set the tone for the rest of your decorations. 2. **Diyas**: As you mentioned, put up the diyas (earthen lamps) in strategic locations, such as the entrance, living room, and verandah. You can also make or buy diyas in advance to save time. 3. **Rangoli designs**: Create or buy rangoli designs to adorn your entrance, floors, or walls. This will add a beautiful and festive touch to your home. **Additional Decorations (Next 1-2 days)** 1. **Flowers and greenery**: Add some fresh flowers, garlands, or potted plants to enhance the festive atmosphere. 2. **Diwali-themed decorations**: Hang Diwali-themed banners, streamers, or balloons to add a pop of color and excitement. 3. **Final touches**: Add any finishing touches, such as decorative items, candles, or lanterns, to complete your Diwali decorations. **Last-Minute Tasks (Day before or Day of Diwali)** 1. **Final cleaning**: Give your home a quick once-over to ensure everything is tidy and ready for your relatives' arrival. 2. **Prepare traditional sweets and snacks**: Make or buy traditional Diwali sweets and snacks to serve to your guests. Remember, prioritize tasks based on your schedule and energy levels. Don't hesitate to ask for help if you need it, and enjoy the festive spirit of Diwali!
